data.name: X4: Foundations
data.detailed_description:
Start Small. Command Everything.

Your journey begins with a single ship - but what you become is up to you.

Trade, fight, explore, and build your way to power as you grow from a lone pilot into the leader of a vast space empire. Command fleets, manage resources, and shape the future of the galaxy through your decisions.

A Living, Simulated Universe

The universe of X4 is fully simulated and constantly evolving.

Factions trade, build, and wage war independently, reacting dynamically to both your actions and each other. Every station, ship, and economy is part of a living system that continues to grow - with or without your influence.

Build Your Empire

Construct space stations, establish trade networks, and control entire production chains.

Design and expand your infrastructure using a modular system, building stations that power your economy, manage supply chains, and automate production as your empire grows into a self-sustaining powerhouse.

Fight and Command

Engage in real-time combat and take direct control of your ships - or command entire fleets strategically.

From small skirmishes to large-scale battles, every encounter is shaped by your tactics and decisions.

A Universe in Motion

  • Thousands of ships and stations carry out their tasks
  • Factions build and expand stations
  • Trade routes evolve as the economy develops
  • Instigate war or broker peace through subterfuge and diplomacy

A Universe That Keeps Evolving

X4: Foundations continues to grow with major updates and expansions that introduce new systems, mechanics, and opportunities for players. Make the universe your own alongside a thriving modding community.

Whether you’re returning or starting fresh, there’s never been a better time to build your empire.

reviews.review:
Since 9.0 I have felt more and more sad about the underlying changes to the jobs.xml for Xenon spawning; So even if you wipe them from the whole map the game's logic forces them to spawn in any random system without ships or regular game rules infrastructure and it does this instead:

Since you want to look under the hood at how the code forces this "stupid shit" to happen, this is what the actual architecture looks like inside the core game files (jobs.xml and the god.xml files).
When you fully wipe the Xenon out of a sector and secure it for real-life days, the game engine triggers a script cycle that completely overrides the sandbox rules. Here is a breakdown of how the game's code "panics" and breaks its own rules:

1. The Global Quota Check (jobs.xml)

<!-- Xenon Economy -->
<product id="xen_energycells" ware="energycells" owner="xenon" type="factory">
<quotas>
<quota galaxy="12" cluster="3" />
</quotas>
<location class="galaxy" macro="xu_ep2_universe_macro" faction="xenon" relation="self" comparison="ge">
<security min="0.75"/>
</location>
<module>
<select ware="energycells" race="xenon"/>
</module>
</product>
</products>

I see these Xenon Energy Cell Factories pop up out of nowhere in places they are always within those five jumps but the Xenon need a natural death and no rebirth mechanic that players can choose; This is 2 weeks of my time every other day; and, I find out the Xenon is cheating abundantly because they are programmed to do so, and they called it a FREE EXPANSION Remember.

quota galaxy="42": This is the literal hard boundary. If you destroy Xenon energy traders and the global count falls below 42, the engine's continuous universe check flags an immediate shortfall. It doesn't wait for standard economic build cues; it forcefully pushes a construction request to any surviving Xenon shipyard or wharf because the explicit condition galaxy="42" is broken.

This is what I am experiencing except there is this: energy trader quota is current and correct and there is also a quota for instant miner building in the xml
<job id="xenon_free_miner_m_mineral_local" name="{20204,1901}">
<modifiers commandeerable="false" rebuild="true"/>
<quota galaxy="36" cluster="6"/>

The tag rebuild="true" tells the script engine that if this specific asset is destroyed, the shipyard queues an identical clone immediately to satisfy the galaxy="36" baseline.

• The "Panic" Trigger: The game runs a continuous universe check. If you destroy a Xenon Energy Trader and the global number drops below the hardcoded quota galaxy="42", the engine completely ignores the state of the universe to fix it. It triggers an emergency initialization function.

2. Bypassing Sector Rules via the "God Script" (god.xml)

So first the Xenon Energy Traders build wharfs and shipyards; They do use OOS tactics to break through blockades and without there being an in-game mechanic to end the Xenon threat entirely since I spent Bazillions fighting the damn Xenon crisis (which I learned is triggered by researching - Fleet-wide Sensor Analytics) If you like getting ravaged by an unending Xenon enemy don't research that for GOD SAKE! PLEASE DON'T DO IT!.

Now every so often I find a Fully built Wharf or Power Station and I never see any ships; Which means the OOS (When you are not looking at the sector, the engine doesn't use physical ships to deliver parts.)

That is basically letting the AI break rules and calling it a win because the game runs faster. Great Expansion again; I love the weapon changes but they don't mean diddly if you can't save the galaxy from the Xenon.

3. Why It Builds From Nothing (The Low Attention Math Trick)

The reason you can sit at the gate with a massive blockade for days and still find a half-built Wharf behind you is due to how X4 calculates building out-of-sector (OOS).

When you are not looking at the sector, the engine doesn't use physical ships to deliver parts. It shifts to a code loop that looks like this:
xml feature example (Example but not proven in the code)
<do_if value="$InLowAttention">
  <add_build_progress station="$XenonWharf" value="$GlobalXenonResourcePool * $TimeDelta"/>
</do_if>



Instead of a physical trader flying past your fleet, the game tracks a "Global Xenon Resource Pool."

This is how the OOS mechanic functions though. As long as that abstract background number ticks upward, the engine simply injects progress percentages directly into the Wharf's code signature.

FIX THAT MAYBE in a 9.1 Hotfix for this Xenon crisis to fully end and not fighting that awful sleeping mega CPU ship

I recommend the game to anyone that does not research Fleet-wide Sensor Analytics, or you can hate yourself, and long as the AI CAN BREAK IT'S OWN RULES, you also have the right to cheat them right back with the help of a mod or two! 

But remember once you research Fleet-wide Sensor Analytics you will play for hours and hours and spend Bazillions fighting a literal endless threat. What ever, the game is amazingly great, until you research Fleet-wide Sensor Analytics, then you might as well punch yourself in tender and fragile place for fun.
